title: Sampling logit equilibrium and endogenous payoff distortion
summary: We introduce sampling logit equilibrium (SLE) for population games in which agents infer payoffs from a finite sample of $k$ opponents' actions and respond according to a logit choice rule. We find that sampling error systematically distorts incentives. Actions whose inferred payoffs are relatively more variable earn a variance premium, while nonlinear payoffs generate a curvature premium through Jensen effects.
